answers.description: A pipeline that transcribes audio files, built modularly so different transcription models can be swapped in.
answers.problem: Model lock-in: transcription tools hard-wire a single engine, so switching models means rewriting the pipeline. Audio Transcriber makes the transcription model a swappable component.
answers.users: Internal team / self — running transcription jobs as part of internal workflows.
goals: Pluggable model backends — any transcription model (local or API) can be added without touching pipeline code.
Accurate, structured output — transcripts with timestamps, speaker labels, and a consistent format across models.
Per-model documentation — for each supported transcription model, document how it is used and what it requires (deps, credentials, hardware).
answers.voice: Concise and direct — short, plain sentences.
principles: Modularity / clean interfaces — model backends behind a stable interface; pipeline code never depends on a specific engine.
Reproducibility — same input plus same config produces the same output; configs and model versions are recorded with results.
answers.backend: None — Python library with a CLI entry point
answers.database: None — transcripts and run metadata written as files on disk (JSON/text)
answers.infrastructure: Self-hosted / Docker — containerized so it runs identically anywhere, including a GPU host
answers.tdd: Flexible — tests recommended for complex logic (backend interface, output normalization); not required everywhere.
answers.commits: Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, refactor:, test:, chore:)
answers.lint_tooling: Ruff (lint + format); mypy optional, not gated
